project_guess: etcd - distributed reliable key-value store using Raft consensus

candidate_flows.name: gRPC Put request
candidate_flows.trigger: Client sends a Put RPC with key-value pair
candidate_flows.why_interesting: This is the most common write path; understanding it reveals how consistency, durability, and concurrency control work.
evidence: wal/encoder.go writes to WAL for durability

candidate_flows.name: Watch stream
candidate_flows.trigger: Client creates a watch via gRPC Watch RPC
candidate_flows.why_interesting: Watch is a key feature for event-driven applications; this flow demonstrates how changes are streamed to clients.

candidate_flows.name: Lease lifecycle (Grant → KeepAlive → Expire)
candidate_flows.trigger: Client grants a lease with TTL, then periodically sends KeepAlive
candidate_flows.why_interesting: Leases are essential for distributed locking and automatic key expiration; this flow ties client and server together.
evidence: lessor.go manages lease grants and expirations

candidate_flows.name: Server startup
candidate_flows.why_interesting: Understanding startup reveals how all components are wired together (storage, Raft, gRPC).

candidate_flows.name: Raft log write path
candidate_flows.trigger: Proposal from etcdserver to Raft (e.g., after receiving a Put request)
candidate_flows.why_interesting: This path shows how proposals are replicated via Raft and written to WAL for safety.
